MAX_CONNS (102) admission and slot eviction that assume RFC 9000 §10.1's 3·PTO floor (a slot held up to 55.6 min, 196 s for a dead peer with defaults).
Retry or a per-source handshake limit (each unauthenticated Initial costs a P-256 signature, ~15 ms, or RSA, 6 ms at 2048 and 45 ms at 4096 bits), or a faster proved exponentiation.

A random-keyed SipHash index for CIDs and reset tokens replaces route's linear scan (up to 512 CID and 816 constant-time token comparisons per datagram, sized for about 100 connections); a sorted Vec is not acceptable (leaks token order, RFC 9000 §10.3.1).

Path slots (MAX_PATHS 4) never evict: an on-path attacker forwarding a victim's packets from spoofed addresses fills them and the client's next NAT rebinding is dropped. Eviction conflicts with wf_amp for paths with logged sends.

An RSA key loader that establishes every rsa_key_wf clause (primality through a verified certificate check, d zero-padded to k octets) before an RSA certificate is accepted; until then a bad key panics or exhausts memory at the first ClientHello that selects it.

Every datagram makes the shell walk all connections (on_wake each loop turn, the target serviced twice): call on_wake only when deadline() <= now; check pipeline::settled_later's ordering assumptions; add a shell test.

Memory per connection may be ~6.4 MiB (REQ_BUF_CAP 65552 x 100 bidi streams), not the ~1 MiB of crates/server/src/lib.rs:100: trace whether reading re-issues credit past the windows, then fix the comment or the limits; a proved per-connection and server memory bound.
Transmit-loop termination is unproved (crates/quic/src/pipeline.rs:316-318); the shell caps polls per wake and, if the cap is ever hit, logs and spins at 1 kHz. Prove termination.

A verified de-amortized byte queue for every quic/tls byte buffer on input paths, so each append and front removal costs O(bytes) worst case with every copy counted, and lazy in-order delivery (owner decision 2026-11-12: per call O(d + log n), d the bytes that call was given): in-order CRYPTO bytes are not copied as a run at fill time (CryptoStream on_fill take_front is O(r) per frame today), nor is Reassembly's in-order delivery; the sites: CryptoStream buf and read (Q4, Q5: take_front appends to buf; Q6 conn.rs copy-and-drop on discard; Q-T1 quictls per-feed read buffer), tls HsReader push and next_message split_off (T1, T2), Reassembly gap fill, split_off and run_end (Q1-Q3), send_stream split_off trim and extend (Q7, Q8), the TLS transcript appends (T3-T5). Sites from the sweep, a grep-driven list not verified row by row.

h3 input costs: the quadratic cookie merge in message.rs build_headers (H1, H2; first, with its RCA), conn.rs reqs/unis updated by remove+insert with linear lookup (H10), request and uni stream buffers front-trimmed by copying the remainder and re-parsed per call (H3, H4, H7), request events (H5, H6), the SETTINGS duplicate scan (H8) and QPACK decode growth (H9). Sites from the sweep, a grep-driven list not verified row by row.
